title: Handoff lanes and acceptance checklist for phased prompt-set rollout with telemetry and privacy gating
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a pragmatic, audit-friendly handoff and acceptance checklist for staged prompt-set releases that collect telemetry. This ticket aligns product, engineering, design, and legal on requirements for: consent language, telemetry schema, opt-out handling, rollout canaries, and final sign-off criteria. The checklist will be used by PMs to drive PRD reviews and by engineers to gate releases in CI/CD and deployment playbooks.
background: We are preparing phased rollouts of new prompt-sets (error-correction, summarization hints) across hosted and dedicated customers. Some prompt-sets will enable lightweight telemetry (event counts, latency buckets, anonymized prompt metadata) to measure regressions. Legal and privacy flagged the telemetry as a potential data-residency and consent risk. Design needs to standardize UI consent copy. Engineering needs clear accept/reject gating criteria to automate canary progression. Current PRDs lack a single cross-team acceptance artifact.
goals: (1) Produce an actionable acceptance checklist that includes legal signoff, UX consent copy, telemetry schema approval, and engineering deployment gates. (2) Define roles and SLA for signoff turnaround. (3) Implement a minimal telemetry opt-out flow and test harness for canary evaluation.
scope_in_scope:
- Acceptance checklist for prompt-set rollouts
- Telemetry schema draft and required anonymization steps
- UX consent copy variants and placement guidance
- Engineering gating steps (canary thresholds, rollback criteria)
- Signoff matrix (who approves what)
scope_out_of_scope:
- Full privacy program changes (e.g., KMS/HSM integrations)
- Long-term analytics pipeline redesign
- Billing or pricing policy changes
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Legal approves telemetry schema and provides a short rationale that can be attached to PRD (signed in Confluence).
AC-2: Design delivers two consent-copy variants and a small interaction spec (modal & account settings) with accessibility review notes.

AC-3: Engineering provides a canary playbook with measurable thresholds (error rate delta, latency p95 delta, token-level quality regression tolerance) and an automated job to evaluate canary metrics.
AC-4: PM demonstrates a dry-run checklist applied to one internal canary rollout and records the steps and audit log links.
AC-5: Checklist lives in PRD template and is linked from the release gating board; signoff steps are machine-readable (labels/status) so automation can enforce gates.
tasks: T1: Draft initial acceptance checklist and telemetry schema (PM).
T2: Legal review of telemetry schema and consent language (Legal).
T3: Design consent UX + accessibility pass (Design).
T4: Implement opt-out flag and minimal telemetry obfuscation pipeline in canary cluster (Engineering).
T5: Create CI job to evaluate canary metrics and post results to release board (SRE/Eng).
T6: Run a dry-run with internal rollout and capture audit artifacts (PM + Eng).
T7: Finalize checklist and add to PRD template; update onboarding doc for PMs (Docs).
decisions: D1: Telemetry will be limited to counts, anonymized latency buckets, and feature flags — no raw prompt storage in canaries.
D2: Consent copy will default to opt-in for new accounts; existing accounts will see a notification with opt-out available in settings.
D3: Canary progression is automated but requires explicit Legal signoff for telemetry-enabled canaries in production regions with data residency concerns.
open_questions: Q1: Do enterprise customers require a separate opt-in flow or an account-level override? (Legal + Sales)
Q2: Which telemetry retention window satisfies both monitoring needs and privacy constraints? (Data + Legal)
Q3: Can the canary CI job access anonymized telemetry from dedicated clusters or do we need a separate ingestion pipeline? (Eng + Infra)
blockers: B1: Legal requested an anonymization proof-of-concept before final approval (assigned to Legal & Data).
B2: Dedicated clusters currently block sampling telemetry out of region — infra task needs a configuration change (ENG-24188).
